fixes.explanation: The land of Cush isn't named anywhere in this message. The text says Egypt and the daughters of the mighty nations go "…to the depths of the earth with those who descend to the Pit…" (Ezekiel 32:18). This isn't a trip to another country. It's a trip down.
Verse 24 says of Elam's multitudes, "They bear their disgrace with those who descend to the Pit." (Ezekiel 32:24). Elam once spread terror in the land of the living. Now disgrace is what they bear.
The text says otherwise, friend. Of Elam's multitudes it says, "They bear their disgrace with those who descend to the Pit." (Ezekiel 32:24). So the statement is True.

The text says, "They do not lie down with the fallen warriors of old, who went down to Sheol with their weapons of war, whose swords were placed under their heads, whose shields rested on their bones…" (Ezekiel 32:27). Meshech and Tubal are set apart from them. So False is the right call, friend.

The text goes the other direction, friend. It says, "But you too will be shattered and lie down among the uncircumcised, with those slain by the sword." (Ezekiel 32:28). The verse says "you" will be shattered, not that "you" will rule.

Might didn't buy Edom a way out, friend. The text says her kings and princes, "…who despite their might are laid among those slain by the sword." (Ezekiel 32:29). The statement is False, because they are laid among the slain.

The text says Edom's kings and princes are those "…who despite their might are laid among those slain by the sword." (Ezekiel 32:29). Their might doesn't keep them out. It's right there in the verse, "…despite their might…"

The text says, "Pharaoh will see them and be comforted over all his multitude…" (Ezekiel 32:31). Pharaoh is the king of Egypt (Ezekiel 32:2). The verse says he is comforted and doesn't tell us why. So I'll leave that open, and just stay with what it says.
